title: Inconsistent metering when proxy rewrites tenant identity header during ephemeral key exchange
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Production incidents observed where tenant-level usage is either double-counted or attributed to a generic proxy account during short-lived API key rotations mediated by an internal broker. Root cause appears to be a header rewrite that replaces the original tenant identity with a proxy principal during proxy rebinds, causing the metering pipeline to emit events tagged to the proxy rather than the originating org/project. This ticket drives a fix and add tests and monitoring to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a workspace W with a service account that delegates ephemeral keys via the internal broker
2) Issue a short-lived API key, then trigger a rotation/rebind by restarting the broker pod
3) Send a steady stream of token-generation requests through the proxy to simulate production traffic (500-2k rps bursts),
4) Observe billing/usage stream (consumer-meter topic) and query attribution for the time window.
observed_behavior: A subset of tokens emitted during broker rebind windows are attributed to tenant id 'proxy-service@infra' or are duplicated as both original tenant and proxy, resulting in overcharging and rate-limiter miscounts.
expected_behavior: All usage emitted for requests should carry the original tenant/project/workspace attribution that matches the API key's ownership, even if a proxy rebind occurs. No duplicate events should be produced for a single logical request.
hypothesis: The broker/proxy performs an identity rewrite to X-Redwood-Principal for internal routing. During rebinds the rewrite path temporarily replaces the canonical tenant header instead of adding a preservation header (X-Forwarded-Tenant). The metering pipeline canonicalizer trusts the first seen principal header, so when the rewrite occurs it incorrectly claims ownership. Race between proxy rewriting and async attribution enrichment causes either loss or duplication of provenance events.
impact_analysis: Affected customers: mid-market and enterprise customers using delegated service accounts via the broker (estimated 4% of active tenants). Measured cost impact on one pilot customer: +12% over a 3-hour window. Operational impact: rate limiter counters tied to project quotas can prematurely throttle legitimate workloads, causing customer-facing errors.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No duplicate meter events for the same request seen in consumer-meter topic during simulated broker rebind tests
2) Attribution of events remains the original workspace even when broker pod restarts mid-request
3) Unit + integration tests added for header preservation and canonicalization logic
4) Dashboard and alerting show rate of 'unattributed' or 'proxy-attributed' events drop to baseline
5) PR reviewed and security review approved.
implementation_plan: A) Short-term hotfix: change proxy middleware to append X-Forwarded-Tenant and avoid overwriting X-Redwood-Principal. Add migration shim in attribution service to prefer X-Forwarded-Tenant if present.
B) Medium-term: update canonicalizer to perform a cross-check against API key metadata from the keystore service when possible to validate header-based attribution (fallback path).
C) Long-term: add signed provenance token in the header for ephemeral keys so downstream services can verify origin without trusting mutable headers.
D) Add end-to-end integration tests that simulate broker rebinds under load (included in CI runtime-integration job).
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy hotfix to staging and run replay harness against real traffic snapshot (2h window)
2) Canary to 5% of prod brokers for 1 hour with live monitoring of 'proxy-attributed' events and billing deltas
3) Promote to 25% after 4h if no regressions, then to 100% over 24h
4) If customer-visible regressions, rollback and open incident bridge.
monitoring_queries: - consumer-meter:SELECT count(*) WHERE attribution='proxy-service@infra' GROUP BY 5m
mitigation: Temporary mitigation for affected customers: opt-in to 'strict-keystore-lookup' via tenant feature flag which forces keystore-backed attribution for all incoming requests (will add ~5-10ms p99).
security_considerations: Header-based fixes must be validated to avoid a header injection vector. Security review requested and included in PR checklist. The long-term signed provenance token design lowers injection risk.
notes: Related work: we've seen similar class of issues when API keys are shadowed by impersonation chains (see ENG-9534). This variant is specific to the broker's proxy rewrite behaviour and occurs under short uptime churn.
